page: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a base speed of 3.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3080.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2066.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Text processing is also strong at 2468.0. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score of 3838.0 and Passmark CPU score of 5402.69 fall into the bottom 25%, as does the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 27.02 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is weak for read-only operations, measuring 294.38 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 38.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth is average at 28.08 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, the F2ams_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for lightweight database operations, caching layers, text processing, and small-scale language model inference, where its average prompt processing speed of 556.46 tokens/sec and text generation speed of 152.1 tokens/sec on a 135M model can be leveraged. However, it is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, or high-throughput web serving due to its lower multi-core and memory read bandwidth performance.
